articles.title_zh: Train collision in Egypt kills 7, injures 112
articles.content_orig:
Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport but the network has suffered repeated deadly accidents
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing seven people and injuring more than 100 others, according to the authorities.
Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The health ministry said 112 people were injured and were now being treated in hospitals around the Giza area.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been asked by three House Republican  committee chairs to brief Congress behind closed doors about his reported ties to a woman accused of spying for China.

articles.title_orig: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.title_zh: Trump unveils 'Iron Gate' task force against Iran as Saudis launch deadly strikes on Houthi rebels
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump told reporters Friday that the U.S. carried out "minor strikes" on Iran, amid reports that two missiles struck Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz.
The missiles struck the island on Friday, Iranian news agency Tasnim reported, according to Reuters . Tasnim said there was no official information on damage, Reuters added.
The island lies off Iran's southern coast, near the Strait of Hormuz, the vital artery for oil and gas that has become a flashpoint in the war.
Speaking to reporters Friday evening after landing in West Palm Beach, Florida, Trump didn't comment specifically on Qeshm Island, saying: "I don't want to talk about it."
But he added: "We do minor strikes, but they knock out. They built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device, and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five." He did not explicitly confirm that he was referring to the reported strikes on Qeshm.
The strikes are the first since Tuesday's midterm elections, after analysts and regional officials had debated whether the vote would lead Trump toward further escalation or renewed diplomacy.
The U.S. struck the same island Monday, in what a U.S. official told MS Now was a " defensive measure ."
Trump also told reporters Friday that Iran wants "to make a deal very badly. They have 300% inflation. Their navy's gone. Their airport, everything's gone, and they want to make a deal."
The International Monetary Fund forecast that Iran's consumer prices would rise by an average of 78.6% in 2026, in a report published Oct. 13.
When asked if he wanted to make a deal "really soon," Trump said: "Well, we have nobody getting hurt, nobody getting killed.
"You know, this is a war that we may have been there for seven months, but we probably fought for three or four weeks, really fought. And again, you look at World War One; that's a war. World War Two; that's a war."
Iran has said it wants more than "paper commitments" from the U.S. before entering a new phase of diplomatic talks.
"We must see practical measures by the Americans," Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state broadcaster IRIB on Friday, according to Press TV .

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Some are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about the matter.
"The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers."
Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.
Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday requesting that he sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang .
The reports refer to Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.
Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, The New York Times first reported on Friday.
When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.
Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO's interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers, the Times reported .
Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump's Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.
Cornyn called the report "outrageous" in his post on X .
Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.
Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC's request for comment.

articles.title_orig: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
articles.title_zh: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
articles.content_orig:
Footage shows derailed train carriages near Giza in Egypt
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.
The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.
Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise.
Uninjured passengers and passersby searched derailed carriages for injured people
The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients.
Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries.
The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed.
The first train involved in the crash was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks.
Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two.
Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains.
The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.
The train continued for around nine kilometres (5.6 miles) before coming to a halt.
In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.
Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.
There were calls in Egypt on Sunday for the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster.

articles.title_orig: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.title_zh: South Africa’s ANC is humbled by its worst election results
articles.content_orig:
South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic".
While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 30.76% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 64.82% 20 years ago.
The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections.
The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 24.64%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town. Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third overall with 9.76%, unseating the ANC as winner in the city of Durban, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), led by Julius Malema, once seen as a serious challenge to the ANC, came fourth with 6.22%.
"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC," said secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on Saturday. "We knew this disaster is coming, we're staring at it. As we got into elections, the cost of living of our people was too high. The middle class have turned on the ANC in big numbers."
Entering the count centre tonight, South Africa's president and leader of the ANC Cyril Ramaphosa said: "We accept the will of the people however concerning it might be, we accept that this is how the people of South Africa in our towns, in our cities, in our metros have spoken - and this is their verdict, we accept it with humility. It is a decline that is concerning, that is how I characterise it."
It's a continuing decline for the ANC, which lost majority rule in the national elections in 2024 for the first time in its history. It then had to form a coalition government with a raft of other parties in what is now known as the GNU, or government of national unity.
While the Democratic Alliance made significant gains in the cities in these local elections, its overall vote share rose marginally from 21.83% in 2021, and was below the 26.9% it gained in 2016.
Voter turnout was 52.29%, an increase from 45.9% in 2021, when elections were held during the Covid pandemic.
"This election is delivering a devastating message to the ANC", said political analyst Susan Booysen. "It's an ANC in decline at local municipal level, at the metropolitan level, and when the results are reflected provincially and nationally, we see severe declines in ANC levels of support all around."
The reason for that decline in support is largely due to poor service delivery and infrastructure across the country, from water and power to sanitation. "These are huge problems," says Booysen, "and have really been affecting the lives of ordinary people, in the suburbs, in the townships, and in very dramatic ways."
The big picture looks even more bleak for the ANC. The party will elect a new leader next year as Cyril Ramaphosa comes to end of his term. He is due to stay on as president of the country until the next national elections in 2029, but there are few candidates lined up to succeed him in either role.
"It is sort of the end of the liberation movement era in South Africa," said political analyst William Gumede, "and the dominance of the liberation movement since the end of apartheid. So the ANC is going to be a party that by 2029 could be the second biggest rather than the biggest party. It may actually spiral into a long period of just total infighting. This is a new era for South Africa's politics and also the ANC."
The elections also saw a significant shift in voting patterns, with the DA, traditionally known as the "white party" for attracting a largely white vote, gaining more black votes. "We're moving towards a post-racial voting pattern in South Africa," added Gumede.
South Africa now faces days of local coalition building, with the three metropolitan municipalities in the province of Gauteng, the country's powerhouse, under particular scrutiny. The ANC may even find itself shut out in the cities of Johannesburg and Pretoria.
"We are now in a coalition country," said Gumede. "Essentially, what the voters are saying is, "Well, the ANC has dominated the last three decades, they didn't use their power to change the society for the good, so we don't want the dominant parties anymore, whether at national level, provincial level, or rather now at a local level. We actually want coalitions. We want people to work together."
Parties now have 14 days from the moment results were announced to negotiate coalitions.

articles.title_orig: 2 big AI narratives wrestle with each other: What to watch this week
articles.title_zh: 2 big AI narratives wrestle with each other: What to watch this week
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Even before the sell-off last week, we've all had the feeling of white-knuckling through the fourth quarter.
Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus. Big Tech earnings. Bond yields through the roof. An unexpectedly tall blue wave that lifted the stock market up — and threw it back down.
With volatility ( ^VIX ) running hot, investors are balancing on a knife's edge between a flywheel of angst — or a bounce.
As Goldman Sachs' panic gauge suggested, the extremeness may signal more of Friday's bounce to come.
It's a new week, and we'll have plenty of scheduled plot points to guide us.
Of particular note, we're looking forward to CoreWeave ( CRWV ) quarterly results on Tuesday and Nebius Group ( NBIS ) and Cerebras Systems ( CBRS ) on Thursday, a few companies caught up in the data center destruction post-election.
What they have to say about their plans and outlook, the debt markets they've been tapping, and the health of their business will be at the top of mind.
Good timing to have that a mere week after midterms.
On the economic calendar, we're in inflation mode once again, especially after that hot jobs report.
We'll kick off the week with the New York Fed's consumer inflation expectations before getting some actual data on Tuesday — and wholesale inflation figures on Friday to close the week.
What's more important: the chip and AI infrastructure trade or the companies that actually provide AI?
As we wrote in the Morning Brief on Friday, "A data center slowdown is bad for the stock market's AI engine," and "A data center slowdown is good for Big Tech's profit machine."
Can Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Amazon ( AMZN ) deliver AI at least some productivity and tools to clients with the compute they have — and make a lot of money doing so, flipping the switch from growth and scale to monetization?
Maybe! Those companies are healthily in the green since the election, doing just fine amid the broader sell-off. And while Tesla ( TSLA ) has sold off, SpaceX ( SPCX ) is mostly doing fine.
As DataTrek's Nicholas Colas wrote on Thursday, you need to look at the entire week, not just the bloody Thursday, to see the bigger picture (small as that is). And it's pretty clear that this may be reflected in the broad indexes, but it's mostly about chips.
"As for what the market is 'saying' over the last 2 days, we believe the moves are AI-centric, not augurs of a looming recession," Colas wrote, also noting that Google and Co. are doing fine.
The push-pull of the chip narrative and the hyperscaler narrative is the pulse our fingers are on right now.
Friday's blowout jobs report of 165,000 jobs delivered an unexpected verdict about the current state of the labor market: It's better than fine.
Even September's underwhelming 29,000 jobs were adjusted upward to 60,000.
Good for breaking the "low-fire, low-hire" ice, if this represents the beginning of a trend. As every Fed chair likes to remind us, one month doesn't mean anything by itself.
The big takeaway from the report, however, isn't that the labor market is heating up, but that any weakness or recession is not currently something to worry about .
But with Tuesday and Friday's big inflation reports for October, we'll have more than just one data point to work with, and two (or more) hot pieces of economic data could start to make some people sweat.
We are keeping one research note from Apollo's Torsten Sløk that caught our attention last week at the top of our mind: that the Fed's rates needed to bring inflation down its 2% target could be as high as 6.75%. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
While the data center sell-off is obviously important, inflation still matters as much as anything.
Bloomberg's average analyst estimate has core inflation rising 0.2%, slowing down from 0.3% last month.
Amid all the data will be a lot of commentary from the people who read the data — and decide what to do with it.
The Fed's Goolsbee and Bowman speak on Monday; Waller and Bowman (again) on Tuesday; Barr, Barkin, and Logan on Thursday; and Williams, Jefferson, and Bowman (again) on Friday.
We love seeing our public officials putting in the work. But the market loves guidance and FedSpeak even more and is hoping to be given more of a lens through which to read all of this data and get a better picture of how the Fed sees the economy — and perhaps even the sell-off, depending on what topics come up and how forthcoming they feel like being.
Right now, after Friday's jobs report, the December hike is feeling more likely.
With Fed Chair Warsh settling into a cryptic, taciturn no-forward-guidance rhythm, it's up to these guys — who may also feel more emboldened post-midterms.
As JPMorgan noted last week , the new Democratic Senate leadership is going to be important for the Fed.

articles.title_orig: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.title_zh: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.content_orig:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone” , in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.
The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.
The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.
The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion
In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.
Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.
The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title_orig: Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh
articles.title_zh: Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh
articles.content_orig:
A building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the financial district of the capital Riyadh has been damaged in a missile attack.
The strike in King Abdullah Financial District has been claimed by the Iran-allied Houthis and came after Saudi Civil Defense issued ‌an early-warning ⁠alert of a potential threat to the city.
Video circulating on social media and verified by CNN shows damage to several floors of the Aramco building, with windows seen blown out. But Saudi authorities said the impact was minimal.
“An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack,” on Sunday, according to the official Saudi news agency, citing a source at the Saudi Energy Ministry.
“The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported,” the agency reported.
However, one witness said they saw ambulances heading to the area.
CNN has reached out to the Information Ministry by email for further details.
The Houthis, who have fired missiles and drones towards multiple targets across Saudi Arabia over the last three months, said in the attack on Riyadh’s financial district was one of several it carried out on Aramco targets. There was no initial comment from Saudi authorities on the additional claims.
The Houthis said they had also targeted Saudi-led ground forces in several parts of Yemen.
The Saudi led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles in Riyadh and the southern region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote in a post on X that air defenses also “intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh.”
The missile attacks on Riyadh came a day after Yemen’s Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi airstrikes had ‌killed ‌at least ​33 ​people near the capital Sanaa, including women and children.
“We will punish the Saudi regime for its crimes against the Yemeni people,” said Mahdi al-Mashat, a senior Houthi official, on Saturday.
Last month, 13 people were killed in one missile strike on Riyadh’s international airport, and several more died in other strikes on the airport.
The Houthis have said they will continue firing missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia so long as the Kingdom carries out airstrikes against the parts of Yemen they control and enforces a blockade against its territory.
Saudi Arabia spent $83 billion on defense last year, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, putting it firmly among the top ten military spenders worldwide. It has acquired US fighter jets as well as Patriot and THAAD air defense systems, and a range of advanced weaponry from France and the United Kingdom.
But the Saudis have a lot to defend: a country roughly one-fifth the size of the US, with threats on three sides - from Iran , Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, and the Houthis.
Iran’s hardliners see a weakened Trump – and want more to end the war
The Saudis are intercepting many of the missiles and drones fired by the Houthis. But some get through . The defense ministry faces difficult choices in distributing the existing systems with so many installations vulnerable to attack.
The Houthis have learned to combine ballistic and cruise missiles with long-range drones to overwhelm Saudi defenses, according to analysts.
In Yemen, the Saudi-backed coalition is trying to prevent the Houthis from advancing further south towards the port of Aden, which is held by the internationally-recognized government.
The Houthis have frequently targeted Aden’s airport with missiles in recent weeks, after taking a stretch of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in September.
Hostilities between the Houthis, who are backed by Iran, and Saudi Arabia reignited in July, shattering a 2022 UN-brokered ceasefire that had largely halted fighting ⁠between the ‌two sides.
Ibrahim Dahman, Teele Rebane and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
A data leak from the Russian state statistics agency Rosstat shows that, according to official figures, over 450,000 Russians have been killed in the war in Ukraine, making the war the fourth most common cause of death in Russia since 2022.
Russia has not officially disclosed its battlefield losses since September 2022 and has dismissed independent estimates as unreliable. Rosstat's figures would make the war in Ukraine Russia's deadliest conflict since World War II, far exceeding the 13,000 Soviet troops killed in the nine-year Soviet-Afghan War.
Rosstat was hit by a cyberattack from Oct.29 and Nov, 1 by the Belarus Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow hacking groups, who posted messages on the organization's homepage. The groups, both banned in Russia as "extremist organizations," stole data on Russia's economy and demographics as well as wartime losses.
"This is the most significant leak of data when it comes to Russian casualties," Janis Kluge, head of the Russia and Eurasia division at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, told The Moscow Times. "I think it's established as a fact that the war has never been more deadly than it is right now." As well as active servicemen, the figure calculated by the Silent Crow includes civilians killed in airstrikes and Ukraine's 2024 incursion into Russia's Kursk region. The total death toll is likely to be higher as this data does not include soldiers missing in action, nor the 27,000 foreign fighters believed to have been recruited into the Russian armed forces.
The Moscow Times cross-referenced a random sample of 50 names from Mediazona and BBC Russian's " Counting the Dead " open source repository of Russian death records with Silent Crow's leaked dataset, but was unable to verify the data in its entirety.
But the figures are in line with other assessments of Russian casualties; the British Defense Ministry said in early September that over half a million people had died fighting for Russia and casualties could number as high as 1.5 million, including the wounded.
Since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, 6.2 Russians have been killed for every kilometer of territory gained. That territory has become increasingly costly each year as the number of registered deaths climbed despite Russia's progress on the front line stalling.
Not all deaths recorded in the database were in combat. 14,160 cases described the death of a member of the Russian armed forces from non-military causes, including illnesses, road accidents or suicide. Over 32,000 died from wounds they had sustained at least a year earlier.
The Belarus Cyber Partisans released a lower figure of 393,881 killed, using a different methodology that only counted the deaths of military personnel or civilians in combat or from the long-term effects of the fighting.
72% of deaths were registered as occurring in the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, where over 20,000 Russian troops were killed in the bloody 10-month Battle of Bakhmut.
The leak supports research showing that Russia's ethnic republics have suffered disproportionately from mobilization and recruitment for the armed forces, with major cities like Moscow registering a smaller share of overall casualties than their populations would suggest.
Researcher Maria Vyushkova told The Moscow Times that the Kremlin's recruitment policies amounted to the "extermination of entire nations" for some of Russia's smallest ethnic groups, attracting men into the armed forces with salaries far more lucrative than anything available locally and generous benefits for their families if they die, or offering a route out of incarceration.
Kluge told The Moscow Times that although Rosstat's figures are dramatic, they may have little economic impact on their own. "This represents around half a percent of Russia's working-age population of 80 million people. That is not enough to make the news because the men who are fighting usually don't have very productive jobs in the first place.
"But the main significance is political," he added. "It's about who is winning this war and you cannot say Russia is winning this war if it is losing population at this rate."
A Message from The Moscow Times:
We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."
These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .
Your support, no matter how small, makes a world of difference. If you can, please support us monthly starting from just $ 2. It's quick to set up, and every contribution makes a significant impact.
By supporting The Moscow Times, you're defending open, independent journalism in the face of repression. Thank you for standing with us.

Investing.com -- Investors are preparing for a busy week on Wall Street, with earnings from five closely watched companies, fresh U.S. inflation data and shifting interest rate expectations likely to shape market sentiment.

The NASDAQ Composite has entered correction territory, falling nearly 12% from its October 6 record, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lost 2.7% and 3.4%, respectively, last week as technology stocks came under pressure and concerns over data-centre spending weighed on risk appetite.
The earnings calendar also comes at a critical time for the technology sector, with investors also preparing for October U.S. inflation data on Tuesday. Economists expect core consumer prices to rise 0.2% month over month, potentially lifting the annual rate to 2.7% from 2.6%. Producer price data due on Friday will provide another test for markets as traders assess the Federal Reserve's next policy move.
Against this backdrop, five companies stand out this week, with their earnings and forward guidance likely to influence sentiment across the broader AI investment theme.
1. Constellation Energy: Powering the AI infrastructure boom
Constellation Energy will kick off the week's earnings calendar with results due before Monday's market open. The electricity producer has emerged as a key beneficiary of growing power demand from artificial intelligence data centres, making its outlook particularly important as investors assess the sustainability of infrastructure expansion.
Its shares closed at $249.95 on November 6, down 30.2% year to date. Analysts expect earnings of $3.72 per share on revenue of $9.21 billion. The company has beaten earnings estimates by approximately 5.8% in each of its previous two quarters.
Investors will focus on electricity demand, long-term supply agreements and management's assessment of data-centre power requirements. Any signs of political resistance to new infrastructure projects could also influence the outlook.
2. CoreWeave: A crucial test for AI computing demand
CoreWeave reports Tuesday after the market closes, with its results likely to provide one of the clearest indications of demand for AI computing infrastructure.
The stock closed at $46.40 on November 6, down 43% over the past month and 59% over six months. Analysts expect earnings of 9 cents per share, although consensus estimates have been cut 12.6% over the past 90 days.
The company's previous two earnings reports triggered sharply contrasting reactions. Shares fell 17.3% following a first-quarter earnings miss before gaining 22.2% after a second-quarter beat.
Investors will closely examine capital expenditure, customer commitments and backlog commentary to determine whether demand for AI computing capacity remains strong enough to justify the industry's substantial infrastructure investments.
3. Nebius Group: A gauge of investor appetite for neocloud stocks
Nebius Group will report before the market opens on Thursday, offering another important assessment of sentiment toward specialised AI cloud infrastructure providers.

Its shares closed at $129.49 on Friday, rising 7.6% during the session but remaining down 41% over the past month. The stock is still up 48.9% year to date.
Nebius shares surged 32% following its second-quarter results and 23.5% after its first-quarter report, highlighting the market's sensitivity to developments in the AI infrastructure business.
Investors will look for updates on capacity expansion, customer demand and financing arrangements as the company scales its operations. Its results could either reinforce or challenge the signals emerging from CoreWeave's report earlier in the week.
4. Applied Materials: Testing the semiconductor spending outlook
Applied Materials, a major supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, will report Thursday after the market closes. Its results could provide insight into whether chipmakers are maintaining investment plans despite growing concerns about AI spending.
The stock closed at $332.72 on November 6, down 34.7% over the past month, although it remains up 44.6% over the past year. Analysts expect earnings of $4.06 per share on revenue of $10.30 billion.
Notably, earnings estimates have risen 10.5% over the past 90 days, making Applied Materials one of the few companies on this week's watchlist where analyst expectations have strengthened despite a sharp share-price decline.
Investors will assess orders, customer spending plans and management's guidance for semiconductor equipment demand to determine whether the sector's weakness reflects a temporary valuation reset or a slowdown in capital investment.
5. Cisco Systems: AI networking demand in focus
Cisco Systems will round out Thursday's earnings calendar with results due after the market closes. The networking equipment maker offers another perspective on the AI infrastructure buildout, particularly demand for networking products connecting increasingly complex data-centre systems.
Its shares closed at $93.85 on November 6, down 18.3% over the past month. Analysts expect earnings of $1.32 per share on revenue of $18.11 billion, while earnings estimates have increased 15.4% over the past 90 days.
Investors will scrutinise AI-related orders, networking demand and profit margins for evidence that the company's exposure to data-centre expansion is translating into stronger financial performance. Any disappointment in AI momentum or margins could intensify pressure on the stock, although improving earnings estimates suggest expectations may be more supportive than recent share-price weakness indicates.
What investors should watch next
The five earnings reports will provide an important snapshot of the AI investment cycle, spanning electricity supply, computing capacity, cloud infrastructure, semiconductor equipment and networking.
The next major catalyst will be Nvidia's November 17 earnings report, which is expected to offer a broader assessment of demand across the AI ecosystem. Until then, investors will look to this week's results and management commentary for evidence that the industry's spending commitments remain intact despite mounting market concerns.

articles.title_orig: UH restores patient access to MyChart system that was shut down by cybersecurity incident
articles.title_zh: UH restores patient access to MyChart system that was shut down by cybersecurity incident
articles.content_orig:
CLEVELAND —     Frustration is growing among some University Hospitals patients as a cybersecurity incident continues to disrupt the hospital system's network more than two weeks after it was first detected.
Patients say they are still dealing with limited access to online services, including MyChart, prescription information, test results and online bill pay.
With many digital services still unavailable, patients are being forced to handle routine healthcare needs over the phone.
Stephen Bloomfield, a lifelong UH patient, says the disruption has made it difficult to communicate with his doctors, manage prescriptions and access important medical information.
"I've never had anything that's gone on quite this long," Bloomfield said. "My bank, my Wi-Fi or email — none of this stuff ever lasts more than a few hours."
Bloomfield says he can no longer access visit notes from his doctor, renew prescriptions online or message physicians through MyChart. He also reports problems with claims processing and scheduling future appointments.
He says even getting someone on the phone has been challenging.
"It was a 20-minute wait on music waiting for them to actually answer the phones," Bloomfield said.
The disruption began October 22, when University Hospitals detected unusual activity on its servers. The health system disconnected its systems from the internet as a precaution while it investigated the incident.
More than two weeks later, some online services remain limited, with patients continuing to report problems accessing their medical information and managing appointments.
Bloomfield says he would like to see more frequent updates from the hospital system about when services might be restored.
"That's what I'd like to see — a little bit more honesty and timeliness with updates as to when this might actually end," he said.
In an updated statement dated November 5, University Hospitals said all of its hospitals; emergency departments and physician offices remain open and fully operational.
The health system says the vast majority of appointments and procedures are continuing. Patients who already have appointments should keep them and do not need to call to confirm.
However, patients who need to schedule appointments, make changes, check on prescriptions or pay bills will need to use alternative methods while online services remain disrupted.
UH says patients will be able to resume paying bills through MyChart once the system is restored.
The hospital system is also warning patients to be alert for scams during the disruption.
UH says it will never call, text or email patients asking for sensitive personal information, including passwords or full Social Security numbers.
Anyone who receives a suspicious call or message should not respond and should instead contact their doctor's office directly.
UH acknowledged that its call centers are experiencing unusually high call volumes and says it is working to increase capacity to handle incoming calls.
For now, patients are being asked to rely on phone calls for many services that were previously available online.
University Hospitals has not provided a specific timeline for when all affected digital services, including MyChart, will be fully restored.
Here is UH's full updated statement:
All UH hospitals, emergency departments and physician offices remain open and fully operational, and our caregivers continue to provide safe, high-quality care. We are experiencing unusually high call volumes in our call center and are working to increase our capabilities to manage incoming calls and continue the highest level of service to our patients.
University Hospitals will never call, text or email you to ask for personal information such as your password or your full Social Security number. If you receive a call or message that seems suspicious, do not respond. Hang up and call your doctor's office.
News 5 promises to Follow-Through and bring you the latest.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Makes the Windows Sticky Keys Dialog Easier to Turn Off
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Makes the Windows Sticky Keys Dialog Easier to Turn Off
articles.content_orig:
It happens on all new Windows PCs: you're playing a game or testing if your keyboard is working properly, so you mash the Shift key a few times. Suddenly, there's a telltale beep, and Windows shows you a message saying that you've enabled Sticky Keys because you pressed Shift five times. A mild annoyance at best, and a game-ending mishap at worst.
The worst part is that the dialog box doesn't give you an easy way to turn it off right there and then. You have to click a link, bring up Ease of Access, and find the setting there. Fortunately, that's about to change, as Windows 11's Sticky Keys dialog will finally let you stop it from the very first encounter.
A few days ago, the Windows 11 Insider Beta Preview Build 26320.9876 landed on people's Insider PCs. Neowin gave the update a spin, and one thing they tested was to see how the new updated handles Sticky Keys.
Sure enough, the new update has subtly changed the dialog box. Beforehand, it would tell you what Sticky Keys was, then offer you a link to the settings page that features its toggle. Now, when the dialog pops up, it will give you a checkbox at the bottom, labelled "Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut." All you need to do is click the checkbox, close the window, and you're done; no more Sticky Keys.
Is it a small change? Yes, very much so. Has it been long overdue? Well, given the number of gamers who have heard the dreaded 'Sticky Keys beep' while in the middle of an intense competitive game (myself included), I'd say it's something that should have been added years ago. Still, better late than never; I'm just glad disabling Sticky Keys has gotten a lot easier.

articles.title_orig: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei’s Argentina
articles.title_zh: Pope wraps up Uruguay visit and heads to most fraught stop of his tour in Milei’s Argentina
articles.content_orig:
FLORIDA, Uruguay (OSV News) — Pope Leo XIV made a pilgrimage to Uruguay’s national Marian shrine Nov. 8, where he shared a message of hope for mothers who feel the grief of seeing their children fall away from practicing the faith they were raised in.
“I know that many of you carry a very specific sorrow. You taught your children to pray, and today they no longer do so. You used to attend Mass together, and it has been years since they entered a church. You spoke to your grandchildren about God, and now you do not know if those words left a mark. Sometimes you wonder if you did something wrong or if it was all futile,” Pope Leo said in his homily.
The pope pointed to the witness of St. Monica, who “prayed for years for a son who seemed to be drifting further and further from God, but she never stopped trusting in his grace.”
“Mothers and grandmothers: never tire of passing on the faith! Preach with your lives as well as with your words. Insist on prayer, love, and hope; insist on them in season and out of season (cf. 2 Tim 4:2). Do so with patience, without harshness or discouragement. Even if your loved ones seem far from God, continue to place them before him. Do not stop blessing them, accompanying them, and simply reminding them of what they once received,” Pope Leo said.
“There are doors that you cannot open, but God can,” he added.
In his homily, the pontiff also offered words of encouragement to fathers and grandfathers, urging them to imitate St. Joseph.
“Dear fathers and grandfathers, young people need to see that you pray, receive the sacraments, treat your wives with respect, ask for forgiveness and live with integrity, even when doing so requires sacrifice. Children learn a great deal by seeing that their father can kneel before God without feeling that he is any less of a man for doing it,” Pope Leo said, to loud applause from those gathered at Mass.
“Your children and grandchildren need to see that the faith occupies a genuine place in the lives of the men in your family,” the pope added.
The pope celebrated an outdoor Mass with 50,000 people in front of the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three , the cathedral basilica of the Uruguayan city of Florida on the morning of Nov. 8, the date of the country’s annual national pilgrimage to the Virgin Mary, which is closely tied to Uruguay’s historic struggle for independence from Brazil.
At this beloved pilgrimage site, Pope Leo renewed the consecration of Uruguay to the Virgin Mary, first made by St. John Paul II in 1988, imploring God that through Our Lady’s intercession “he may thwart the works of the evil one and preserve beloved Uruguay from whatever might lead it away from Christ.”
The unique Marian title of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three takes its name from the image from the 33 revolutionaries whose 1825 campaign sought to free the territory then known as the Eastern Province from the Brazilian Empire.
The Assembly of Florida, which declared independence Aug. 25, 1825, met beside the town’s church, and its members venerated the Marian image preserved there.
“This small image is linked to a decisive moment in Uruguay’s history. In 1825, those who were fighting for the freedom of this land also turned to Mary, to place the beginning of their efforts under her protection. That gesture reminds us that the history of peoples, too, cannot be fully understood without reference to God,” Pope Leo said.
“Since that time, generations have come and gone, circumstances have changed, including the relationship of many Uruguayans to the faith. Yet she has remained here.”
The current cathedral basilica in Florida building was built in 1887, but the wooden image of the Virgin Mary preserved inside the national shrine traces its history back further to the late 18th century and has become closely associated with Uruguay’s national story. Carved from Paraguayan cedar, it is a small representation of the Immaculate Conception believed to have originated in the nearby Jesuit missions.
“This devotion did not originate in any miraculous event or an apparition, as many Marian devotions do,” Father Gabriel González Melano, a priest of the Diocese of Florida, told OSV News.
“It was the people who began to identify her with that campaign,” Father González said. “From 1825 onward, they gradually began to call her the Virgin of the Thirty-Three, with many also dubbing her the liberator of Uruguay.”
Martín Lage Ponce de León, who came on pilgrimage to the shrine with his family from the capital city of Montevideo, told OSV News that Our Lady of the Thirty-Three “represents a lot for all the people in Uruguay.”
“We are really excited about receiving Pope Leo,” he said. “It’s something that we are really grateful that he chose Uruguay to start his trip in South America. And we consider that this is because of something Uruguay really needed … his words of mission.”
Twenty-six-year-old Ximena Tejeria watched eagerly from her wheelchair as Pope Leo greeted the crowd of thousands waving Vatican flags from the popemobile. “This is my first time seeing the pope,” she said of Pope Leo. “I previously met Pope Francis, and now we get to see (Pope Leo) up close, which is wonderful for all of Uruguay, too. It’s been many years since a pope visited, so this whole event is a source of joy for everyone.”
Natalia Baccino, 45, from the capital city of Montevideo has made many pilgrimages to Florida’s Virgin in her life, but this was the first papal Mass at the shrine.
“I woke up really early at 4:30 a.m. to arrive here because … the routes, there were too many people coming here,” Baccino told OSV News.
The pope traveled about 60 miles by car from Montevideo to arrive at the shrine. The road included one pit stop to pray in the parish of St. Thérèse of the Child Jesus, or Santa Teresita, in Juanicó, to greet the mayor and to offer a blessing to people gathered there.
“The principal reason for Leo visiting the shrine is, of course, that the pope is coming to Uruguay, so he had to visit the country’s patroness,” Father González said. The convergence of her feast and the national pilgrimage, he added, makes the occasion particularly significant.
St. John XXIII authorized the image’s canonical coronation in 1961 and declared Our Lady of the Thirty-Three patroness of Uruguay in 1962. In 1975, Uruguay’s government designated the cathedral and the image national historic monuments, and in 1994 the cathedral became the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three.
At the end of Mass, Bishop Alfonso María Bauer Ormazábal of Florida told Pope Leo, “We are a country of close-knit communities, of sharing mate , and of gatherings of friends. And that country was born here, in Florida: next to the so-called ‘Altar of the Motherland,’ our Independence was declared, under the gaze of the Virgin of the Thirty-Three.”
“Today, we face different struggles , and we ask Mary to accompany us in these as well:
the poverty of so many children and the lack of work, loneliness and a sense of meaninglessness, addictions and mental health issues, social fragmentation, and violence. With her, we wish to defend the dignity of every person, daughter and son of God,” the bishop said.
The Mass in Florida marked the final public event of Pope Leo’s Nov. 7-8 visit to Uruguay. After Mass and lunch with local bishops, he is scheduled to fly to Buenos Aires, Argentina, where he will meet President Javier Milei in the afternoon.
Uruguay’s national Marian shrine is one of three Latin American pilgrimage sites Pope Leo is visiting during his Nov. 6-17 tour of South America .
In Argentina, Pope Leo is expected to celebrate Mass at the Basilica of Our Lady of Luján, the country’s national Marian shrine. In Peru, he intends to visit Zaña, where relics of St. Turibius of Mogrovejo, the missionary archbishop of Lima and patron of the Latin American episcopate, are preserved.

articles.title_orig: Apple Taking New Approach to Developing iOS 28 and macOS 28
articles.title_zh: Apple Taking New Approach to Developing iOS 28 and macOS 28
articles.content_orig:
Apple has made a change to its development process for iOS 28, macOS 28, and corresponding software updates, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman.
In his Power On newsletter today , he said Apple separates development of each year's new operating systems into three major stages. Typically, he said each stage consists of four weeks of coding followed by a four-week "convergence" period where new features are integrated into the operating systems. This time around, Apple has made a change.
The first stage of development for iOS 28 and the other updates apparently consisted of six weeks of coding and two weeks of feature convergence. This change gives Apple's software engineers more time to come up with new features.
"Instead of the normal split between two four-week efforts, Apple engineers were tasked with six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development, and then only two weeks of convergence," he said. "Employees say they like the change, indicating that it creates more time for coming up with ideas and exploring them before needing to lock things in."
Gurman did not reveal any specific features planned for iOS 28. The update should be available in beta in June and released in September next year.

articles.title_orig: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100 others, authorities said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 32 miles south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry. One of the trains derailed, it said, but did not specify which.
The Health Ministry said at least four people were killed and 88 others were wounded. The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, it said.
A train driver was among those killed in the collision, the Health Ministry said.
President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi said in a social media post he is following the aftermath of the train collision "with great concern and extend my deepest condolences to the families of those who lost their lives."
"I have directed state agencies to provide the necessary medical care, promptly investigate the circumstances of the accident and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent," he wrote.
Emergency teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, the Egyptian Railway Authority said.
Last September, a train driver and his assistant were injured after two freight trains collided in the same district.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

articles.content_orig:
crim has released El Shaddai: Zero Nine Reversi , “a board game that puts a bold twist on classic Reversi,” for PC via Steam at a 10 percent-off launch discount price of $3.59. The price will change to $3.99 after November 15.
El Shaddai: Zero Nine Reversi first launched for iOS via App Store and Android via Google Play on April 27. The mobile versions were updated alongside the PC release today with online multiplayer support and an archive.
Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page :
Zero Nine Reversi is a board game that puts a bold twist on classic Reversi. Every stone has HP.
The game includes two ways to play: “Classic,” a deep single-player challenge, and “Online,” where you pick a character and battle other players.
In normal Reversi, flipping a stone is the end of the story. In Zero Nine Reversi , a flipped stone loses 1 HP. When its HP reaches zero, the stone is purified and vanishes from the board. This simple change turns every match into a battle of attrition, where positioning, timing, and resource management matter as much as territory.
A versus mode where you choose a character and fight. On top of stone HP, it adds the “BUMP & BURST” rules and a unique ability for each character.

articles.title_orig: Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy
articles.title_zh: Apple CEO Presses Software Chief to Pursue More Ambitious AI Strategy
articles.content_orig:
In the past few years, a major Apple story (especially in the age of AI) has been that the company isn’t moving fast enough in the space to keep up with competitors. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman , new Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly pushing on software chief Craig Federighi to ‘accelerate’ Apple’s roadmap for software.
At the moment, there’s no indication that Apple’s well known software SVP Craig Federighi will be leaving the company. In fact, Craig has made it a very low priority of his to develop a succession plan in any sense, per Mark Gurman . That said, Ternus still wants to see change in how Craig Federighi thinks about Apple’s software strategy:
In recent weeks, Ternus held a closed-door meeting with Craig Federighi, who became Apple’s AI czar following last year’s dismissal of its former AI leader. Desiring more and frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors, Ternus pushed his software chief to accelerate the company’s road map and move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri.
A large part of Federighi’s approach has been how hands-on he is, resulting in his viewpoint shaping how Apple’s software development goes to a large extent. That’s left team members feeling that they have ‘limited influence’ over what happens:
Federighi is known for taking an especially hands-on role in meetings and major decisions, with some employees describing a management style that can leave little room for competing ideas to gain traction. He is also known for vigorously debating opposing viewpoints, using his command of technical details and ability to argue his position to push back against proposals he disagrees with. That approach has at times frustrated members of the software engineering and design teams, some of whom believe they have limited influence over the direction of products.
Another part is that Federighi reportedly only plans for a 12-18 month timeframe, versus the years-long roadmaps used in hardware engineering. These are some of the gaps that Apple may want to bridge in the coming years.
Separately, Vision Pro and Siri AI leader Mike Rockwell is still seriously considering stepping down. He’s currently vice president of Siri engineering:
The management concerns go beyond Federighi. Mike Rockwell, who created the Vision Pro headset in addition to leading the development of Siri AI, continues to seriously consider stepping down. That could mean leaving his role as vice president of Siri engineering — or Apple altogether — next year. Such a move would be a major blow, given his role in bringing the new Siri to market after an embarrassing two-year delay.
In the same report, Gurman also reported that Apple is experimenting with a new development pipeline, giving engineers 50% more time to code and explore more, and spend less time on integration, as coding agents have improved.
It remains to be seen what else might change at Apple to enable faster development timelines, though it seems likely that Craig Federighi may have to release his ‘firm grip’ on the software engineering org, and instead allow some other leaders to blossom and act on their own accord.

Windows 11 is getting another substantial batch of changes in November, but after going through what's coming, two improvements stand out to me: the customizable context menu and Cloud Rebuild.
The first finally gives you control over some of the clutter that has plagued Windows 11's right-click menu, while Cloud Rebuild offers a much easier way to reinstall Windows without creating a bootable USB drive.
Those are only two of the 11 changes worth knowing about this month , which also include improvements for handheld gaming, Phone Link , accessibility , Edge performance, security, and more.
Availability will vary because Microsoft rolls many features out gradually , but here's what you should be watching for in our latest Windows 11 guide .
Here's all you need to know about the features and changes coming in November.
Starting with the November update, Windows 11 is getting a new context menu experience that gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear in the main menu.
The new menu reduces clutter and makes the experience faster by moving app extensions into a separate submenu. It also introduces a "Customize menu" option at the bottom of the interface, which opens a dedicated Settings page where you can enable or disable built-in commands, add options such as "Print" and "Send to," and control which app extensions appear in the main menu or submenu.
You can also display "Cut," "Copy," "Paste," "Rename," "Delete," and "Share" as individual commands instead of showing them in a vertical view. Windows 11 also lets you move "Properties" to the bottom of the menu as it appeared on Windows 10 .
To access these options, right-click a file, folder, or the desktop and select Customize menu , or open Settings > Personalization > Context menu .
You can keep the default configuration if you prefer. Holding down "Shift" while right-clicking also reveals the legacy context menu.
The ability to customize the menu is particularly useful because it gives users more control over which commands they see without forcing everyone to use the same layout.
Microsoft is also refreshing the Gaming Task View experience in XBOX mode. The updated interface retains the familiar design but adds a navigation bar that makes it easier to access options such as "Exit to Desktop" and "Power Options" using a game controller.
It's a relatively small change, but it makes basic actions easier to navigate using a gaming controller.
The Settings app is getting a few usability refinements. The "Privacy & security" page now groups Location, Microphone, and Camera controls more clearly, making it easier to review these permissions.
Microsoft is also expanding the "Device Info" card on the "Home" page to more markets. Available to users signed in with a Microsoft account, the card provides an overview of key hardware specifications and a shortcut to the "About" page.
The "Storage" page is also getting visual changes to its temporary files section.
These aren't major additions, but they make some commonly used Settings pages easier to navigate.
Phone Link integration is getting a small convenience improvement. When your phone is connected, you can hover over a recent message or notification in the Start menu 's "Recent" section of the mobile pane to preview its contents without opening it.
It's a minor addition, but it makes checking incoming messages more convenient without opening your phone or the Phone Link app.
The Magnifier feature is getting three useful improvements, including independent zoom levels for multiple monitors, viewport locking, and a new contrast theme. These additions give you more control over magnified content while making it easier to work across multiple displays.
The biggest improvement is per-monitor zoom, which lets you assign a different magnification level to each display. For example, you can keep one monitor at 150 percent and another at 200 percent.
The feature is enabled by default, but displays must use "Extend" mode. Adjust each screen with the Magnifier toolbar or shortcuts (" Windows key + Plus/Minus "). Viewport locking keeps one magnified screen fixed while you move the pointer to another. Use " Ctrl + Windows key + K " to lock/unlock or " Windows key + Esc " to release all. A new dark contrast theme reduces glare while keeping colors intact. Enable it from the Magnifier toolbar or Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier. Color inversion is separate.
The Narrator feature now supports reading and navigating math equations, making it easier for people with low vision to understand formulas, equations, and scientific notation.
The feature works with supported Microsoft 365 apps, including Word and PowerPoint, as well as web content in Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome .
You can use it with the "Narrator key + Alt + N" shortcut to enable math navigation, and then use the arrow keys to explore individual parts of an equation. Use the "Esc" key to exit. Math reading supports six languages, including English, German, Spanish, Finnish, and Traditional Chinese.
You can change the language and other preferences under Settings > Accessibility > Narrator > Math reading .
Browser support requires Microsoft Edge version 153.0.4234.32 or later, or Google Chrome version 153.0.8010.18 or later.
Windows 11 is making recovery easier by allowing the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles saved in the main operating system.
This allows computers to connect automatically to supported wireless networks during recovery operations such as Quick Machine Recovery and Cloud Rebuild, without requiring administrators to configure Wi-Fi credentials separately during recovery.
The feature is enabled by default and supports certain certificate-based enterprise networks, though it doesn't currently support TPM-backed certificate keys. Network administrators can turn off the capability through the Recovery Configuration Service Provider (CSP) .
WinRE only accesses saved network credentials when a recovery operation requires connectivity, rather than maintaining a permanent network connection.
I've been testing Cloud Rebuild , and eliminating the need to create installation media is easily its biggest advantage. However, I also ran into an important limitation: the feature depends on Windows Update having the drivers your PC needs.
Unlike a traditional local reinstall, it doesn't depend on the existing Windows installation or require a bootable USB drive or a custom recovery image. You can also start it from the Windows Recovery Environment when the device cannot boot.
You can start the process under Settings > System > Recovery and use the "Rebuild this PC" option, or from WinRE by selecting Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud Rebuild . After connecting to Ethernet or Wi-Fi, the system will display the target build, edition, and language before installation.

articles.title_orig: A ‘Chaotic Race’ for the World’s Top Diplomat
articles.title_zh: A ‘Chaotic Race’ for the World’s Top Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
Rebeca Grynspan of Costa Rica extended her lead in the race for United Nations secretary-general in yet another informal ballot held by the Security Council. The two new candidates that joined the contest recently struggled to get the minimum of nine “encourage” votes.
In the straw poll on Thursday, Nov. 5, Grynspan got 12 encourage ballots, one higher than the last straw poll, on Oct. 30, according to multiple leaked results seen by PassBlue. The number of “discourage” votes for her also dropped to three, but she needs to get zero discourage, including no veto, for the Council recommend her as the nominee to the General Assembly.
In Thursday’s undifferentiated straw poll, it is unclear which Council members cast a discourage vote against Grynspan, though there is plenty of speculation that it has consistently been the US throughout the series of informal balloting and possibly Russia this time — both veto holders. A color-coded ballot reveals vetos from a permanent member (Britain, China and France as well), but not who cast them.
No date has been set for another straw poll or whether it will be color-coded. (The only such poll in the race so far was held on Oct. 16.)
Lana Nusseibeh , a candidate from the United Arab Emirates (who was born in 1978), and Feridun Sinirlioglu , 70, of Türkiye, are the newest entrants in the race. From the start of her nomination, announced on Oct. 21, Nusseibeh has been facing strong pushback from civil society groups as the media also scrutinize her country’s enabling role in the war in Sudan and its related atrocities.
The New York Times reported on Nov. 5 that UN investigators had linked an Emirati security company to the country’s ruling family to deploy Colombian mercenaries alongside the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group fighting the Sudanese Armed Forces in Sudan’s civil war. Nusseibeh, who until recently was a top UAE diplomat, has over the years repeatedly denied Emirati support of the RSF.
Soon after she announced her candidacy as UN secretary-general, Human Rights Watch questioned whether she would defend the independence of UN investigative bodies examining her government’s actions in Sudan and elsewhere.
The UAE authorities also repeatedly reject allegations that they support either side in Sudan’s war, despite numerous UN independent inquiries and other expert institutions saying otherwise. That includes a Human Rights Council’s fact-finding mission report published in September, saying the UAE has “played a significant role in networks involved in the recruitment, financing, transportation and deployment” of foreign military contractors and the provision of military-related support benefiting the RSF.
Nusseibeh is saying in her campaign that ending the conflict will be a priority if she is selected UN chief. But human rights experts say that even if she commissioned an independent UN inquiry into the Sudan war, as the head of the UN, it could be challenging for her to separate such a step from her country’s own geopolitical ambitions.
Sinirlioglu announced his candidacy on Oct. 30. He is a former foreign minister, UN ambassador and currently the secretary-general of the Organization for the Security and Cooperation in Europe. In Thursday’s straw poll, he received three encourage, eight discourage and four “no opinion” votes, far below the threshold to be a viable contender. Like another candidate in the race, Olara Otunnu of Uganda, the Turk was included in the Council’s informal ballot before he met with the General Assembly, a formality in which the other nominees have participated.
The public dialogue for Sinirlioglu is scheduled for Nov. 6, and an informal, private meeting with Council members is planned for Nov. 9.
An outside expert on the UN race told PassBlue that China may be insisting for now that the informal polling remain undifferentiated rather than color-coded to give more time to candidates from the Latin American region — of which there are five — to drum up more support while Beijing continues to assess Nusseibeh.
In May, China’s representative at the UN told reporters that his country preferred that a woman — without specifying who — should clinch the top UN post and that the selection process should abide by the UN’s regional rotation system. (The UN has never been led by a woman, and the Latin American-Caribbean area says it’s their turn for the job.)
In Thursday’s poll, Rafael Grossi of Argentina remained second, with nine encourage, four discourage and two no opinions, reflecting no change from the Oct. 30 balloting. Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett of Guyana also retained her same spot from the last poll, with eight encourage, but her discourage numbers fell to five from six and she drew two no opinions, one more than last time.
Otunnu got four encourage, nine discourage and two no opinions. María Fernanda Espinosa, backed by Antigua and Barbuda but an Ecuadorian, received three encourage, 10 discourage and two no opinion. The results of the Tonga-nominated Ivonne A-Baki (also Ecuadorian) remained unchanged: One encourage and 14 discourage.
The second term of Secretary-General António Guterres ends on Dec. 31.
Damilola Banjo is an award-winning staff reporter for PassBlue who has covered a wide range of topics, from Africa-centered stories to gender equality to UN peacekeeping and US-UN relations. She also oversees all video production for PassBlue. She was a Dag Hammarskjold fellow in 2023 and a Pulitzer Center postgraduate fellow in 2021. She was part of the BBC Africa team that produced the Emmy-nominated documentary, "Sex for Grades." In addition, she worked for WFAE, an NPR affiliate in Charlotte, N.C. Banjo has a master's of science degree from the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism and an undergraduate degree from the University of Ibadan in Nigeria.
We would love your thoughts. Please comment:
The race for the next Secretary General is now a competition between candidates over who can be the most anodyne.  Venality and the collective abrogation of responsibility by the leaders of the P-5 and by the many and varied sheep in the General Assembly has brought us here.  Not even the stalwart supporters of the UN system have risen to its defence and insisted on better.  Not a peep from the Nordics.  Utter silence from Canada.  Acquiescence from South Africa.  The list goes on…
But it gets worse. Fully 7 members of the Security Council judge Ms. Nussebeih of the UAE to be a suitable candidate for UN Secretary General even though, on the evidence, she is just about the closest one can get in international relations to being an adjudicated liar.  Is this a firm foundation for the highest level of diplomacy?
These are shameful days for the purported stewards of the Westphalian state system.  Historians in every language will look back in amazement on these times.  And they will surely ask, “How could they have been so stupid?”.
Thank you again Damilola/Pass Blue. Easily the best reporting on the UNSG race.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.content_orig:
Former military chief says prime minister brought Israel to historic crisis and it is approaching ‘point of no return’
Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task of forming a government on Sunday, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he said the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.
Eisenkot, 66, the leader of the Yashar party, who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from the president, Isaac Herzog, who gave him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.
“We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the state of Israel,” said Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie at a ceremony at the presidential office. “We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps.”
Eisenkot faces significant challenges on the road to becoming prime minister. He has three options: a power-sharing agreement with Netanyahu, support from Arab-led parties – something several members of his bloc do not support – or an agreement with the ultra-Orthodox parties, which demand military exemptions for their community.
Eisenkot and Herzog acknowledged Israel’s growing isolation under Netanyahu, who is wanted by the international criminal court.
In the US, Israel’s closest ally, Democrats on Tuesday swept the midterm elections, with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war, which Netanyahu launched with Donald Trump.
Eisenkot said: “We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed.”
He appealed to Netanyahu’s Likud party as well as the far-right party of the finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, to join him – but only with himself as prime minister.
“My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment,” he said.
Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a coalition, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier.
Eisenkot’s wide-ranging opposition bloc won 48 of the Israeli parliament’s 120 seats in the October elections, while Netanyahu’s camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.
During party consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received the endorsements of both Arab-majority lists, who could now play kingmakers after making unprecedented gains in the vote.
Eisenkot has laid out a series of conditions for any Arab party to join his coalition, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and declaring the Palestinian militant group Hamas a terrorist organisation. One of his partners, the more conservative Yisrael Beiteinu party, has already said it will not join a coalition with Arab-led parties.
Eisenkot, a former army chief, and his partners made equal military service a central part of their campaign. Specifically, they are seeking an end to the longstanding draft exemptions enjoyed by the ultra-Orthodox.
Netanyahu has repeatedly claimed the election was “stolen” by Arab parties , which rallied their supporters to vote in large numbers. But he has offered little to no evidence to support the claims.
after newsletter promotion
Netanyahu is expected to continue his pressure tactics against Eisenkot, saying any alliance with the Arab parties would be an act of betrayal.
Israel’s Shin Bet security agency has launched an investigation into possible foreign interference in the vote, but the country’s Central Elections Committee – and Herzog – say the vote was valid and even if wrongdoing was found, it did not have a significant impact on the result.
Netanyahu called for a “national unity” government with Eisenkot on Saturday night but it remains unclear whether the two rivals could agree on a power-sharing agreement. These types of coalition governments are notoriously fragile and often collapse.
Eisenkot, the military chief of staff from 2015 to 2019, has set out to unite Israelis after Netanyahu’s divisive tenure, under which the country moved sharply to the right.
He has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity, decrying recent incidents as “Jewish terror” abetted by Netanyahu’s government.
He opposes the creation of a Palestinian state and has vowed to end Hamas’s rule in Gaza and destroy the Islamist movement’s military wing.
Commanding the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah, Eisenkot devised the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”. The idea, named after a Beirut suburb heavily damaged in that war, involves Israel vowing to use massive force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by the Lebanese militant movement Hezbollah.
After his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.
If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections. The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 owing to repeated deadlocks.
